deep.reconstruction: The page holds no recoverable mathematics. It is a very faint pencil draft written only in the right half of the sheet. The left half is blank, apart from two specks. The legible structure is a heading 'III.' followed by a short sub-heading of about two lines, which seems to start with a dash and end with a long dash. After that come numbered items '1.', '2.', '3.' and possibly '4.'. Several lines are struck through: one inside item 1, one in item 3, and the last full line near the bottom. A bracket in the left margin joins two lines in the lower block. Most lines end in dashes, which is typical of a list of section headings or a working plan rather than a derivation. I cannot reliably read individual words. Fragments such as 'Begriff', 'Fläche' or 'Function' are conceivable but unconfirmed, so I do not propose any wording. No formulas, symbols, equations or computations are visible. Context: the next folio (44r) is a draft of Riemann's 1851 dissertation 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. It treats branch points (Windungspunkte) of the covering surface T, the definition of a function on T, and §6, the boundary-integral theorem ∫(∂X/∂y − ∂Y/∂x)dT = ∫(Y cos ξ − X cos η)ds. The most plausible reading of this page is therefore an outline or table of contents (part 'III' with sub-points 1–4) for a section of the dissertation or a related draft. This is my inference from layout and context, not from legible text. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.

results.what: Probable outline or plan (heading III with numbered points 1-4) for a section of a draft related to the 1851 dissertation; content illegible
